candidates.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
candidates.abstract: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel detection achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.95, while vessel localisation has a median error of around 300 m for vessels longer than 100 m, and vessel AIS type-code classification achieves 62% accuracy for the majority classes. The latter, however, is highly correlated with vessel length. These results reveal both the potential and current limitations of Geospatial Foundation Models (GeoFMs) when applied to fine-grained MDA understanding in real-world scenarios. Additionally, a new maritime remote sensing dataset is released, pairing about 2,000 Sentinel-1 images with temporally aligned AIS signals from commercial vessels. Through manual inspection, each candidate sample was verified for bounding-box quality and for consistency between the AIS-reported vessel length and the observed vessel extent, cross-checking vessel identity and location against publicly available vessel records and, where available, photographs. The dataset was made ready for use with the NeuCo-Bench neural compression benchmark framework, publicly available on HuggingFace through https://huggingface.co/datasets/embed2scale/S1-single-ship-downstream .

candidates.title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels at https://github.com/tingrui-huang/timestamps-matter.

candidates.title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
candidates.abstract: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. When prescriptive proverbs take a consistent stance, they favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception, and kindness over malice, and show a moderate tendency toward suspicion over trust. On dimensions involving genuine trade-offs, especially autonomy versus compliance, proverbs provide contradicting advice rather than a single recommendation. This analysis provides a quantitative map of the collective prescriptions in a culture's proverbial wisdom, revealing a core of prudent, honest, and forward-looking guidance alongside varied advice where circumstances dictate the best course of action.

candidates.title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
candidates.abstract: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved. Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable, while direct preference optimization may alter capabilities inherited from the teacher. We propose a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) that addresses both limitations. We estimate the curvature required for PBRF using a surrogate proxy dataset, removing dependence on the original transfer corpus, and extend the framework to preference-based supervision through an odds-ratio objective. This enables the use of preferred and dispreferred response pairs while constraining changes to the distilled model. Our results show that the proposed approach improves targeted trustworthiness behaviors for both pre-training and post-training models while largely preserving downstream performance, providing a practical alternative to re-distillation or unconstrained preference optimization. Our experiment results show that across different distilled models, the trustworthy regression can be improved by up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.

candidates.title: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy?
candidates.abstract: Many languages of instruction in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are poorly represented in the data used to train language models. Before these models can support early-grade literacy in such languages, we need to know whether they hold the linguistic knowledge of each language that literacy teaching relies on. To test this, we present the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark and the reproducible, largely automated pipeline that turns curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books into a vetted question set organised on a fixed grid of nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. The pipeline combines LLM-driven source survey, feature consolidation, item generation and quality control with an item-selection step inspired by item response theory and a final expert review. We instantiate it for Kiswahili (Kenya; 135 items) and English (United Kingdom; 137 items) and evaluate 121 and 119 models respectively. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but accuracy falls steeply for smaller and cheaper models, and more so in Kiswahili. The two best models under 10 billion parameters reach 91.7% and 73.0% in English but only 51.9% and 40.7% in Kiswahili, and the mean accuracy of models deployable on mobile and tablet hardware is 47% in English against 24% in Kiswahili. The models most practical for low-resource classrooms are therefore the least capable in the languages they would serve. We release a 20-item sample per language, all pipeline prompts, open-source code, and a public leaderboard. This is the first rung of a three-level evaluation ladder for measuring and generating decodable text to support foundational literacy.

candidates.title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
candidates.abstract: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures revisit layer parameters across depths. This design increases effective depth without adding parameters. Recent looped MoE studies report substantial gains over the standard MoE at matched budgets (parameters, FLOPs and KV cache). However, the reported gains still confound parameter revisit with other design choices, e.g., network shape and residual scale. We ask, what does parameter revisit itself buy? Using matched non-revisit controls, we find that parameter revisit itself buys almost nothing. We argue that revisit only offers a freedom an MoE already has, i.e., trading experts for depth (more layers, fewer experts each) at fixed parameters. First, at matched budgets, we decompose the state-of-the-art looped recipe, with revisit last. A non-revisit control retains all the gain. Most comes from network shape, and the rest from residual scale. We prove this scale acts as a lower learning rate on revisited layers. This helps under AdamW's uneven layer step sizes, but disappears under Muon, which keeps them nearly equal. Second, beyond matched budgets, we evaluate revisit by adding compute at fixed parameters. One extra visit gains more than doubling the experts. Yet without revisit, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute obtains 90.2% of that gain under Muon. Overall, gains come from network shape, the optimizer and added compute, which a standard MoE can adopt. Accordingly, we propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger MoE baseline. Under Muon, it matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scale. We open-source LoopTitan and release 17 pretrained models (including LoopTitan-Base and the control). Our experiment record is public as GitHub issues, with predictions pre-registered and the full exploration history kept. This is our Phase 1 technical report, laying the foundation for follow-up studies.

candidates.title: Interfaces in Long Range CFT$_1$
candidates.abstract: We consider interfaces in the theory of a single free scalar in AdS$_2$ defined by adding relevant operators along portions of the boundary. We begin with Neumann/Dirichlet interfaces, computing the associated scaling dimension and $g$-factor ratio; we also explain how arbitrary interface correlators can be computed numerically efficiently. Then we move on to interfaces between generalized free field and long-range interacting theories such as long range Ising, determining many quantities in perturbation theory. Finally we setup a bootstrap problem for four-point interface correlator. We use this to find tight bounds on the $g$-factor ratio as a function of the interface scaling dimension.

candidates.title: The all-loop spectrum of GGK strings
candidates.abstract: We study the non-perturbative spectrum of the non-relativistic limit of string theory in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, also known as GGK theory. In light-cone gauge, we show that the bosonic spectrum on a number of vacua is described at all-loops by free massive and massless scalar fields in AdS$_2$, confirming a conjecture by de Leeuw, Fontanella and Nieto-García, arXiv:2403.09563. In static gauge, we obtain the same result for any classical string vacuum, and including fermions. We compute the quantum correction to the classical energy, and show that it vanishes once we adopt the regularised Hurwitz series. We conclude that the quantum energy spectrum built upon any GGK string consists solely of its classical vacuum energy.

candidates.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
candidates.abstract: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed position-space representation of the two-point function for the chosen stable vacuum sector, including the contribution fixed by the CCR in the unstable sector. The resulting expression exhibits the direct and reflected singularities, including Robin-dependent logarithmic terms. Since the remaining unstable contribution is smooth, all states in the constructed family share the same singularity structure, consistent with the Robin--Hadamard framework.

candidates.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
candidates.abstract: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\toμ^+μ^-$ and $K_L\toπ^0ν\barν$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.

candidates.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
candidates.abstract: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,μ,τ$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_μ-L_τ$ force from neutron star binaries.
